Electoral Commission 
The Commission has published their first Report on Ireland’s Electoral Registers. 
It reviews the status of the accuracy and completeness of electoral registers, and of 
how they are managed and maintained by Ireland’s 31 local authorities (see pages 
11-12). 
 
St. Patrick’s Day Visit to New York 2025 
The President of the Kildare Association of New York, Mrs Carmel Mangan, recently 
invited Councillor Kevin Duffy, Cathaoirleach of Kildare County Council, and Annette 
Aspell, Deputy Chief Executive, to New York for St Patrick’s Day.  Meetings were 
arranged with IDA Ireland and Enterprise Ireland.  There were also a number of 
official engagements with the Kildare Association of New York (see pages 12-16).

Municipal Art Collection on Loan to the National Gallery of Ireland  
An artwork from Kildare's Municipal Art Collection was requested for inclusion in a 
hugely significant exhibition of two pioneering female artists regarded as among the 
most important Irish artists of the twentieth century, Mainie Jellett and Evie Hone 
(see page 18). 
 
Affordable Housing Delivery 
The Council is delivering eight affordable houses at Lattin Place, Rathasker Road, 
Naas; the scheme will deliver five number three bed units and three number two bed 
units (see page 25). 
 
Integration - Clinics 
Kildare LAIT organises regular drop-in information clinics in IPAS and BOTP centres, 
that allow service users to access Integration Support Workers on a one to one 
basis.  This has fostered strong relationships between service users, 
accommodation providers, and other services (see pages 37-38).

Secondary, Regional and Local roads throughout the county. Included in this work

road marking renewals and the delivery of the Road Opening Licence system (see 
page 62).

St. Patrick’s Day Visit to New York 
2025 
The President of the Kildare 
Association of New York, Mrs Carmel 
Mangan, recently invited Councillor

Association of New York in the St. 
Patrick’s Day Parade.  The parade 
started at 11.00am and was truly a 
spectacle as 200,000 people marched, 
many behind their Home Counties

Kildare Association of New York 
Meet and Greet 
Pictured below – the Cathaoirleach 
and Deputy Chief Executive with 
members of the Kildare Association

It was a pleasure to meet with the 
Kildare Association, New York who 
hosted a dinner in Yonkers, New York.  
The dinner was an opportunity for the 
Committee and members of the 
Association to meet the deputation 
from Kildare.  Each of the Committee 
officers were presented with a 
selection of gifts from “Gather” in 
Kildare Town, together with gifts 
relating to St Brigid. 
 
It was also a huge honour to visit the 
graves of Jack Murray (1877-1932) 
and his brother Michael Murray (1882-
1957) Calvary Cemetery, New York 
this week. Calvary Cemetery is the 
final resting place of the legendary 
John “Jack” Murray, who captained 
Kildare to their first All-Ireland title in 
1905. 
Jack was knocked down by an 
autotruck and fatally injured August 
16th,1932 in Manhattan aged 55. He 
shares his final resting place with his 
brother Michael, who died in 1957 
aged 75 and also played on the 
victorious 1905 Kildare team. 
Captain Jack Murray was from the 
Rosberry Club (now Sarsfields), 
named after the townland in which 
once stood Sarsfield’s castle. The 
team included another eight players 
from Rosberry, among them Jack’s 
younger brother Michael Murray and 
his first cousin Thomas Keogh.  
Rosberry won their first championship 
in 1904 and would go on to complete 
seven-in-a-row up to 1910, though the 
county would have to wait until 1919 
for a second appearance and victory in 
the 1919 All-Ireland. 
We discussed the potential of 
commemorating these two amazing 
Kildare men and the achievement of all 
this 1905 County Team with the 
Kildare Association, New York.

Citizen Science Fish Doorbell 
At Clocha Rince Library, we are 
participating in the Visdeurbel (Fish 
Doorbell) citizen science initiative from 
March to June, inviting patrons to 
watch a live stream from a canal in 
Utrecht (NL) and ring a virtual doorbell 
when they spot migrating fish. This 
helps alert lockkeepers to open the 
sluice gates, supporting fish migration 
and biodiversity. In April, we were 
delighted to welcome Willemijn 
Koppelaars, a city ecologist from 
Utrecht, who visited the library to share 
the project’s ecological importance and 
inspire local children to engage with 
environmental science. This project 
supports the strategic goal in the 
Councils corporate plan of Climate 
Action, Resilience and Environmental 
Protection.
